series.label: EDL grid supply, national average hours per day (official statements and press, dated points)
series.notes: Not a clean series: each point is a dated statement. Ranges are stored as midpoints. 2021-07: 3-4 h, since mid-2021 (Ministry of Energy and Water plan, https://energyandwater.gov.lb/mediafiles/articles/doc-100777-2022_03_31_10_18_39.pdf). 2022-03: about 4 h for 500 MW supply (same plan). 2023-06: 3-4 h (IMF Article IV, https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2023/237/article-A001-en.xml). 2024-08: 5-6 h when 600 MW is available, 1-2 h on 200 MW (L'Orient Today, https://today.lorientlejour.com/article/1423036/lebanon-flirts-with-blackout-again.html). 2024-12: 4-6 h, rising to 6-8 h over the holidays after +200 MW at Zahrani (https://today.lorientlejour.com/article/1440942/edl-announces-it-will-supply-6-to-8-hours-of-power-per-day-during-holiday-season.html). 2026-02: 7-9 h at end February 2026, per the Energy Minister as reported by Libnanews; 2026-07: about 4 h, official EDL figure of 13 July (Libnanews 9 Sep 2026, https://en.libnanews.com/electricity-in-lebanon-promises-against-cuts/). Secondary reporting of official statements; EDL has begun publishing smart-meter data on feeders but no machine-readable file was found.

series.label: Typical EDL supply hours per day before the 2019-21 collapse (survey recall and EDL range)
series.notes: HRW survey (n=1,209, Nov 2021-Jan 2022): respondents recalled about 12 h of EDL per day before the crisis; HRW also states EDL gave 12 to 21 h a day until 2021 depending on region. A recall estimate, not a measurement.

series.label: EDL hours per day received by households (HRW survey, Nov 2021-Jan 2022)
series.notes: Average household received EDL for about 10 percent of the day (2.4 h); the median household got 2 h. Same survey: average 9 h per day with no electricity from any source (vs about 1.5 h before the crisis); South Lebanon 7 h, Beirut and Mount Lebanon 11 h.

series.label: National grid hours per day reported by Syrian refugee households (VASyR)
series.notes: UNHCR/UNICEF/WFP VASyR, households connected to the grid; self-reported, not metered, and the sample is Syrian refugee households (VASyR 2021: https://ialebanon.unhcr.org/vasyr/files/vasyr_chapters/2021/VASyR%202021%20-%20Energy.pdf).

series.label: Private generator hours per day reported by Syrian refugee households (VASyR)
series.notes: VASyR 2021 and 2022, among households with a generator connection (65 percent in 2021, 47-48 percent in 2022). Self-reported.

series.label: Power-cut hours per day reported by Syrian refugee households (VASyR)
series.notes: VASyR 2021: 3 h in 2019, 5 h 24 min in 2020, 6 h 30 min in 2021 (64 percent of households reporting cuts); VASyR 2022: 15 h 11 min on average (97 percent). The definition changed between rounds; read the trend, not the exact step.

series.label: EDL supply hours per day, Beirut urban area
series.notes: IMF country report (Oct 2019), citing EDL: Beirut urban area received 21.2 h per day. Year not stated in the extract; 2018 data assumed (low confidence on the year).

series.label: EDL supply hours per day, Bekaa region
series.notes: Same IMF report: Bekaa 12 h per day. Year assumed 2018 (low confidence on the year).

series.label: National grid hours per day, Akkar (refugee-household report)
series.notes: VASyR 2021: lowest in Akkar (2 h 35 min). Self-reported, Syrian refugee households.

series.label: National grid hours per day, North governorate (refugee-household report)
series.notes: VASyR 2021: North 3 h 28 min. All governorates except Bekaa had under 9 h. Self-reported, Syrian refugee households.

series.label: Generation capacity, as reported (installed, available or effective: see notes)
series.notes: 2018: 2,512 MW total (EDL plants 1,884 + barges 388 + Syrian imports 240), World Bank 2020 market assessment (https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/353531589865018948/pdf/Distributed-Power-Generation-for-Lebanon-Market-Assessment-and-Policy-Pathways.pdf); peak capacity 3,456 MW. 2020: 2,670 MW installed (thermal 2,381, hydro 282, renewables 7), JICA report. 2022: about 2,300 MW installed excluding hydro, about 2,000 MW effective (Ministry plan, https://energyandwater.gov.lb/mediafiles/articles/doc-100777-2022_03_31_10_18_39.pdf). 2024: no more than about 1,800 MW national production capacity, an expert quoted by The National (23 Aug 2024, https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2024/08/23/why-does-lebanon-have-no-electricity/), a low-confidence figure. Definitions differ between points; this is not a consistent series. 2026: EDL reported about 1,000 MW of grid capacity missing in summer 2026 (https://en.libnanews.com/electricity-in-lebanon-promises-against-cuts/); no absolute level given, so no point.

series.label: Peak demand (EDF least-cost plan)
series.notes: EDF "Least Cost Generation Plan" for the Ministry of Energy and Water: 2019 observed (about 3,844 MW), 2020 estimated, 2021-22 projected on its base case (3,717 and 3,393 MW), so these are modelled values. Annual demand 24,247 / 24,339 / 23,979 / 21,890 GWh.

events.title: Rationing deepens
events.detail: EDL cuts output after the central bank stops paying fuel shipments; a harsh rationing schedule starts.

events.title: Beirut port explosion hits EDL
events.detail: EDL headquarters destroyed and the national grid control centre lost; control moved to Bsalim.

events.title: Karpowership barges stop
events.detail: Two Turkish power barges (370 MW) stop supplying over payment arrears.

events.title: Supply falls below 4 h/day
events.detail: EDL average supply drops to under 4 hours a day from June 2021.

events.title: Nationwide blackout
events.detail: Zahrani and Deir Ammar shut down for lack of fuel, leaving no centrally generated electricity.

events.title: First tariff increase since the 1990s
events.detail: EDL tariffs raised for the first time since the 1990s.

events.title: Distributed Renewable Energy Law passed
events.detail: Parliament passes the law; it awaits the Electricity Regulatory Authority.

events.title: Total nationwide blackout
events.detail: Last operating plant shuts after EDL runs out of fuel (delayed Iraqi swap shipments); more than 24 hours without public electricity.

events.title: Algerian fuel shipment
events.detail: Algeria sends several thousand tonnes of fuel to restart the plants.

events.title: Holiday supply increase
events.detail: EDL commissions +200 MW at Zahrani, lifting supply from about 4-6 h to 6-8 h a day. Only Zahrani and Deir Ammar run; Zouk and Jiyeh idle.

events.title: 7-9 hours a day
events.detail: EDL reaches 7-9 hours a day by end February 2026, per the Energy Minister.

events.title: About 4 hours a day, collapse warning
events.detail: EDL reports a national average of about 4 hours and warns of a possible general collapse because about 1,000 MW of capacity is missing.

notes: Events are blackout and supply milestones. Series ids ending _m are monthly. See README-D3.md.
